plain: The wall mixes a storage cost (an SU(N) link needs 2N states, so more than one qubit) with a readout artifact (no colour-labelled pattern is colour-neutral) and a real gap (nothing forms multi-site links). Reading the wall's own model through colour-blind local labels, the non-abelian Gauss law becomes a local parity rule on record patterns and the dynamics stays local, so colour is not invisible; what remains is forming and hosting those label registers.
best_route: R1: use colour-blind local labels (matter count, link orientation, one local pair-Casimir label at busy vertices) as the records; the Gauss law is then a Z_N centre-parity star constraint, which reduces T27 to T77, T10 and register hosting.
test: Five finite scripts on the wall's own SU(2) model plus star, valence-6 and SU(3) vertices: baseline reproduced (0/65536 patterns, 82 singlets, E0=-sqrt34); all 1296 atoms have Gauss rank 0 or 1 and the 82 rank-1 atoms are exactly the parity-rule atoms; hop is single-link local; on a 4-link star 64 atoms have rank 2 and one local pair Casimir resolves them; all passed.
cheaper_question: Can the Z_N centre-parity star constraint plus vertex registers of at most 5 states be hosted on Z^3 sites, one qubit per site, under nearest-neighbour formation and cubic covariance (T77, T10)?
